Any retinopathy caused by variants in the SPATA7 gene.
Folliculitis of the beard and/or mustache areas caused by a bacterial infection, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus.

Myasthenia gravis characterized by the presence of autoantibodies against the muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (AChR) in the serum, which damage the postsynaptic neuromuscular junction and cause skeletal muscle weakness and fatigue.
Myasthenia gravis in which the muscles around the eyes are affected, that typically presents with ptosis and/or diplopia due to ophthalmoplegia
Myasthenia gravis characterized by the presence of autoantibodies against muscle-specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) in the serum

synonyms.val: myasthenia gravis caused by muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibodies

definition.val: Myasthenia gravis characterized by the absence of detectable pathogenic auto-antibodies against acetylcholine receptor (AChR), muscle-specific tyrosine kinases (MuSK), and/or low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 4 (LRP4) in the sera.
Myasthenia gravis in which muscle weakness affects one or more skeletal muscle groups outside the extraocular muscles

Any disorder of oxysterol accumulation caused by biallelic loss of function variants in the CYP7B1 gene. A disorder of oxysterol accumulation is a condition where there is an abnormal buildup of oxysterols, which are oxidized cholesterol derivatives, in the body.

A rare neurologic disease characterized by neonatal hypotonia, global developmental delay, feeding difficulties, and often seizures or seizure-like episodes. Other frequently observed signs and symptoms include variable dysmorphic features, myopathic facies, respiratory problems, and visual abnormalities, such as strabismus or esotropia. Brain imaging may show delayed myelination and other white matter abnormalities.

nodes.lbl: PLEC-related muscular dystrophy-epidermolysis bullosa simplex spectrum disorder

definition.val: A spectrum of disease associated with loss or disrupted function of the PLEC gene. These disorders primarily affect the skin and muscles, leading to a range of symptoms including skin blistering (EBS), progressive muscle weakness (muscular dystrophy), and other complications.

synonyms.val: PLEC-related muscular dystrophy-epidermolysis bullosa simplex spectrum disorder
qualitative or quantitative defects of plectin

definition.val: A disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of HDAC4 and is characterized by brachydactyly type E, variable mild to moderate intellectual disability, seizures, autism spectrum disorder, short stature, obesity, and facial dysmorphism. Individuals with the gain of functions variants typically do not have brachydactyly and do have more consistent intellectual disability.

comments: This term is more specific because it includes brachydactyly that is not characterized in the parent term. https://www.clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40006/

nodes.lbl: SAMD9L-related spectrum and myeloid neoplasm risk

definition.val: A susceptibility or predisposition to myeloid neoplasms in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SAMD9L gene. This condition is characterized by variable presentations of ataxia and cytopenia, myelodysplastic syndrome, monosomy 7 (acute myelogenous leukemia), and bone marrow failure.

synonyms.val: SAMD9L-related spectrum and myeloid neoplasm risk

definition.val: A genital ulcer characterized by the rapid onset of painful, necrotic ulcerations of the vulva or lower vagina. It typically occurs in sexually inactive adolescent females or young females and may be preceded by influenza-like or mononucleosis-like symptoms. Acute genital ulceration has been associated with acute Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection or other viral and bacterial infections. However, in many cases a cause cannot be determined.

comments: This term is specific to non-sexually transmitted and sudden onset of genital ulcers.

definition.val: Any ciliopathy in which the cause of the disease is a variant in the TUBB4B gene. Please note that patient diagnoses can include disorders such as Leber congenital amaurosis and/or primary ciliary dyskinesia.

nodes.lbl: FDXR-related optic atrophy mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome

definition.val: Any mitochondrial disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FDXR gene.

synonyms.val: FDXR-related optic atrophy mitochondrial dysfunction syndrome

nodes.lbl: MYCBP2-related developmental delay with corpus callosum defects

definition.val: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the MYCBP2 gene. This condition is characterized by variable corpus callosum defects consistent with dysgenesis, and a broad spectrum of neurobehavioural deficits including developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autistic features.

synonyms.val: MYCBP2-related developmental delay with corpus callosum defects

nodes.lbl: ACO2-related optic atrophy with or without extraocular features

definition.val: An optic atrophy in which the cause of the disease is monoallelic or biallelic variants in the ACO2 gene. ACO2 is a mitochondrial protein and thus, in addition to the optic atrophy features, features of this disease include abnormal mitochondrial morphology and can affect other organ systems. Extraocular features can include ataxia, spastic paraplegia, CNS abnormalities, neurodevelopmental phenotypes, and retinal degeneration.

synonyms.val: ACO2-related optic atrophy with or without extraocular features

definition.val: An invasive adenocarcinoma characterized by the presence of focal or extensive transformation of malignant glandular cells to squamous epithelial cells.

nodes.lbl: autosomal dominant polycystic kidney and/or liver disease-ALG8

definition.val: An autosomal dominant disease caused by variants in the ALG8 gene that is characterized by incomplete penetrance and a range of clinical manifestations, spanning from individuals with normal kidneys to those with numerous kidney cysts and chronic kidney disease (CKD). While the common presentation involves a limited number of kidney cysts and maintained kidney function, severe polycystic liver disease (PLD) with minimal kidney involvement (ADPLD) can also occur.

synonyms.val: ALG8-related autosomal dominant polycystic kidney and/or liver disease
autosomal dominant polycystic kidney and/or liver disease-ALG8

definition.val: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variation in the GRIN1 gene. It is characterized by mild-to-profound developmental delay/intellectual disability (DD/ID) in all affected individuals. Other common manifestations are epilepsy, muscular hypotonia, movement disorders, spasticity, feeding difficulties, and behavior issues. A subset of individuals show a malformation of cortical development consisting of extensive and diffuse bilateral polymicrogyria.

A rare, life-threatening fetal condition resulting complete or partial obstruction of the fetal upper airways. Laryngeal atresia is the most frequent cause, but other etiologies, such as laryngeal cyst, subglottic stenosis or atresia, tracheal atresia, and laryngeal or tracheal agenesis are also included.
A form of Cushing syndrome caused by prolonged exposure or excessive use of cortisteroids, usually from medications taken to treat other conditions.
Any orofacial cleft in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ARHGAP29 gene.
Any cardiovascular disease resulting from atherosclerosis.

A group of disorders caused by a variation in PIK3R1 gene that produces a structurally altered but present p85α protein, disrupting PI3K signaling and leading to features such as immune deficiency, autoimmunity, short stature, and distinct facial and skeletal features.

A group of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding subunits of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor, including GRIN1, GRIN2A, GRIN2B, and GRIN2D. These disorders are associated with a spectrum of symptoms such as developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy, movement disorders, speech and language impairment, and neuropsychiatric features. The clinical presentation and severity vary depending on the specific gene and mutation involved.

A group of neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders caused by variants in the GRIN2A gene, characterized by a broad spectrum of symptoms including developmental delay or intellectual disability, epilepsy, speech and language impairments, movement disorders, and neuropsychiatric features.

nodes.lbl: GRIN2A-related developmental and/or epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep

definition.val: Any developmental and/or epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep in which the cause of the disease is a variation in GRIN2A gene.
Any rolandic epilepsy-speech dyspraxia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in GRIN2A gene.

nodes.lbl: GRIN2A-related self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes

definition.val: Any self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes in which the cause of the disease is a variation in GRIN2A gene.
A digenic form of retinitis pigmentosa resulting from a mutation in the PRPH2 gene and a null mutation of the ROM1 gene, leading to progressive degeneration of the retina and vision loss.
A Leber congenital amaurosis that is caused by a variation in the PRPH2 gene.
Any Pfeiffer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR1 gene.
Any Pfeiffer syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the FGFR2 gene.

A rare iatrogenic disease characterized by paradoxical nasal obstruction and symptoms including air hunger and suffocation-like breathing sensation, nasal dryness and crusting, burning pain or cold airflow sensation, impaired sleep and cognitive function and severe anxiety and depression, and typically occurs after surgical reduction or removal of nasal turbinates.

comments: ENS is often misdiagnosed as psychiatric in origin due to the disproportionate suffering compared to physical exam findings. ENS results from disruption of normal nasal airflow dynamics, mucosal sensory feedback, and humidification, typically after aggressive surgical intervention on the nasal turbinates. Estimated prevalence: <1 in 10,000, though underreporting and misdiagnosis likely make this an underestimate. ENS is currently considered a rare, post-surgical complication, with cases reported globally but concentrated among ENT surgical patients. No universally accepted biomarker exists. Diagnosis is based on symptoms, medical history and imaging. There is no cure. Symptom management includes nasal moisturization (saline gels, humidification), nerve modulating agents (e.g., amitriptyline, gabapentin) nasal implants to restore airflow resistance and cognitive-behavioral therapy and psychiatric support. ENS most often develops after surgery and is considered an iatrogenic condition because its other causes also result from medical interventions, such as electrocautery or laser procedures that cause turbinate trauma.

definition.val: A rare semidominant genetic skeletal disorder caused by a variation in ACAN gene, characterized by short stature with variable phenotypic features which may include osteochondritis dissecans, advanced bone age, early-onset arthritis, and/or features consistent with spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, Kimberley type caused by a single allele whereas biallelic variation can cause spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, aggrecan type.

A disease characterized by a spectrum of cardiac and extracardiac phenotypes caused by a disease-causing variant in the NOTCH1 gene, inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. Affected individuals may present with congenital heart defects, bicuspid aortic valve, aortic valve stenosis, thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection, anomalies in brain structure, intracranial or posterior circulation vascular anomalies, cutaneous vascular malformations, cutis marmorata, and/or a phenotype compatible with Adams-Oliver syndrome (i.e. cutis aplasia, terminal limb defects, skull ossification defects).

comments: Variants in NOTCH1 have been reported in individuals with the following disease entities: Adams-Oliver Syndrome, congenital heart disease, aortic valve disease including bicuspid aortic valve, and thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. Individuals with pathogenic variants in NOTCH1 may also be asymptomatic due to incomplete penetrance and extensive intrafamilial variability. Per criteria outlined by the ClinGen Lumping and Splitting guidelines, we found no difference in molecular mechanism and inheritance pattern and found considerable interfamilial and intrafamilial variability in cardiac phenotypes. Therefore, Adams-Oliver syndrome 5 and aortic valve disease 1 have been lumped into one disease entity (NOTCH1-related AOS spectrum disorder).

definition.val: A schizoaffective disorder marked by episodes of hypomania or mania and sometimes major depression.
A schizoaffective disorder marked by episodes of only major depression.

nodes.lbl: multiple symmetric lipomatosis with partial lipodystrophy

definition.val: A form of multiple symmetric lipomatosis accompanied by partial lipodystrophy (loss of subcutaneous fat in other regions), with or without peripheral neuropathy. Nearly all reported cases have been observed in individuals who are homozygous for the p.Arg707Trp variant in the MFN2 gene.

A skeletal ciliopathy caused by a mutation in INTU gene and is characterized by facial dysmorphism, tongue nodules, developmental delay, and polydactyly. Some individuals may also present with short stature, or other variable syndromic findings.

nodes.lbl: complex movement disorder with or without neurodevelopmental features

definition.val: A movement disorder characterized by having one or more different types of movement disorders, such as abnormal muscle tone, abnormal degree of movement, dystonia or torsion, which may occur with or without neurodevelopmental features, such as developmental delay or intellectual disability.

synonyms.val: complex movement disorder with or without neurodevelopmental features

definition.val: A form of distal renal tubular acidosis that is inherited.
A form of distal renal tular acidosis that develops secondary to another condition, usually disease or drug.
Any neutropenia in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ELANE gene.

comments: ELANE-related neutropenia includes congenital neutropenia and cyclic neutropenia, both of which are primary hematologic disorders characterized by recurrent fever, skin and oropharyngeal inflammation (i.e., mouth ulcers, gingivitis, sinusitis, and pharyngitis), and cervical adenopathy. Infectious complications are generally more severe in congenital neutropenia than in cyclic neutropenia.

nodes.lbl: giant cell hepatitis with autoimmune hemolytic anemia

definition.val: A rare autoimmune disease of early childhood, marked by the simultaneous or sequential immune attack on red blood cells and liver cells.

comments: Giant cell hepatitis–autoimmune hemolytic anemia (GCH-AHA) presents as a combination of autoimmune hemolytic anemia and giant cell hepatitis, with potential to involve other organs over time. Though its exact cause is unclear, the condition reflects a broader immune system dysregulation. It can be transient or chronic, and while treatment remains complex, advances in understanding its immune basis have led to improved management and prognosis.

synonyms.val: giant cell hepatitis associated with autoimmune hemolytic anemia
giant cell hepatitis with autoimmune haemolytic anaemia

nodes.lbl: HAVCR2-related subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and/or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis predisposition

definition.val: Hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the HAVCR2 gene, which confers the predisposition to susceptibility to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (SPTCL) and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). Affected individuals typically present with multiple subcutaneous nodules and systemic B symptoms.

synonyms.val: HAVCR2-related subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and/or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis predisposition

definition.val: A diffuse midline glioma characterized by H3 K27 alteration and usually either a histone H3 K27M mutation, an EGFR mutation, or aberrant overexpression of EZHIP. The prognosis is poor.

comments: Currently, diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27M-mutant is the single child term. Other child terms will be added during Mondo alignment with NCIT.

definition.val: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in FAM111A gene.

nodes.lbl: FLNB-associated autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder

definition.val: Any autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in FLNB gene.

synonyms.val: FLNB-associated autosomal dominant filamin related bone disorder

nodes.lbl: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QA

definition.val: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QA gene.

synonyms.val: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QA

nodes.lbl: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1S

definition.val: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1S gene.

synonyms.val: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1S

definition.val: A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by the variants in the RNU2-2 gene, in which most reported variants are de novo. It is characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, autistic behavior, and characteristically complex seizures.

An autoimmune disorder that involves a constellation of psychiatric and neurologic symptoms that present simultaneously and in rapid onset, the cause or causes of which are unknown. Although the cause is still under investigation, the manifestations may follow a recent infection.

nodes.lbl: RNU5B-1 related neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and joint laxity

definition.val: A neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in RNU5B-1 gene and is characterized by global developmental delay, hypotonia, macrocephaly, failure to thrive, abnormality of the eye, seizures, and joint laxity

synonyms.val: RNU5B-1 related neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and joint laxity
neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures and joint laxity

definition.val: A glioblastoma localized in the brain stem.
Any propionic acidemia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in PCCA gene.
Any propionic acidemia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in PCCB gene.
Hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the EGLN12 gene, which confers a predisposition to erythrocytosis and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma.

nodes.lbl: systemic lupus erythematosus related to PLD4

definition.val: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the PLD4 gene.

synonyms.val: systemic lupus erythematosus related to PLD4

definition.val: A variant of parapsoriasis characterized by round-to-oval plaques less than 5cm in diameter, and it rarely progresses.
A variant of parapsoriasis characterized by erythematous-to-brown patches or thin plaques with fine scales larger than 5cm in diameter. It has a substantial risk to evolve to mycosis fungoides.

A hereditary amyloidosis characterized by a spectrum of neurodegenerative and neurovascular phenotypes caused by pathogenic variant in the APP gene, resulting in an abnormal clearance of amyloid peptides, either by overproduction and decreased clearance of amyloid peptides, with deposition of amyloid in plaques and blood vessel walls. Affected individuals may present with progressive cognitive decline, cerebral vascular amyloidosis with white matter changes, and stroke with or without hemorrhage.
Any ciliopathy caused by variants in the IFT74 gene.

A syndromic disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CASK gene. It is associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum ranging from mild-to-severe intellectual disability with or without nystagmus to moderate-to-profound intellectual disability and progressive microcephaly with pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, often associated with seizures.

nodes.lbl: X-linked intellectual disability with or without nystagmus

definition.val: An X-linked intelelctual disability in which the cause of the disease is hypomorphic CASK pathogenic variants. Affected individuals present with intellectual disability with or without congenital nystagmus. Additional features often include epilepsy, speech impairment, motor delay, and variable brain malformations. Phenotypic severity ranges from mild cognitive impairment to severe developmental disability.

An autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome that results from defective lymphocyte homoestasis, and is caused by variants in the FAS gene. It is characterized by non-malignant lymphoproliferation, autoimmune disease, and lifelong increased risk for both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
A predisposition caused by a mutation in SH2B3 gene that presents with myeloproliferation and/or multi-organ autoimmunity.

nodes.lbl: congenital heart disease with heterotaxy syndrome

definition.val: A heart disease that is present at birth that occurs with variable extracardiac laterality defects. Features of visceral heterotaxy are not always present but can include abnormal location of the organs within the thoracic, abdominal, or peritoneal cavities. Anatomic and functional problems can include intestinal malrotation leading to volvulus, biliary atresia, and various defects of the central nervous system, urinary tract, and skeleton.

synonyms.val: congenital heart disease with heterotaxy syndrome

definition.val: A stroke disorder caused by obstruction of blood flow to the brain, due to thrombotic (local blood clot formation) or embolic (due to a blood clot or other material traveling from another site) event.

A stroke disorder caused by bleeding into the brain parenchyma or surrounding spaces. Hemorrhagic stroke includes intracerebral hemorrhage (bleeding within the brain tissue) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (bleeding in the space between the brain and the surrounding membrane).

A form of hyperthyroidism caused by overproduction of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) due to pathology within the thyroid gland itself. Primary hyperthyroidism is characterized by low TSH levels and elevated T3/T4 levels.

A form of hyperthyroidism caused by overproduction of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) due to pathology outside of the thyroid gland, namely in the hypothalamus or pituitary gland. Secondary hyperthyroidism is characterized by elevated TSH levels and elevated T3/T4 levels.
A condition in which a single benign adenoma on the thyroid gland  autonomously secretes excessive thyroid hormone, leading to primary hyperthyroidism.

A form of secondary hyperthyroidism caused by pathology in the hypothalamus leading to excessive stimulation of the pituitary gland and subsequent overproduction of TSH, resulting in elevated thyroid hormone levels.
A disorder of the female reproductive system characterized by abnormalities in the menstrual cycle, including disturbances in timing, flow, or associated pain.
A menstrual disorder characterized by pain during the menstrual cycle.

A form of dysmenorrhea characterized by recurrent menstrual pain without any identifiable underlying pelvic pathology, representing a diagnosis of exclusion. Symptoms typically emerge within two years of menarche.
A form of dysmenorrhea associated with suspected or clinically identifiable pelvic pathology, such as endometriosis, uterine fibroids, or adenomyosis.
A form of amenorrhea defined by the absence of menstruation by the age of 15 years, or by 3 years after the onset of breast development (thelarche).

A form of amenorrhea characterized by the absence of menses for 3 or more months in a woman with previously regular menstrual cycles, or 6 or more months in any woman who has had at least one previous spontaneous menstruation.

A form of secondary amenorrhea caused by suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis without identifiable organic pathology, typically associated with energy deficiency, excessive exercise, psychological stress, or low body weight.

A reproductive system disorder caused by a variation in the NR5A1 gene, and characterized by varying phenotypes, including partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis, ambiguous genitalia, and spermatogenic failure in the male, and premature ovarian failure and ovarian dysgenesis in the female.

comments: 46XY individuals can present with azoospermia, hypospadias, micropenis, cryptorchidism, ambiguous or female-appearing genitalia, partial or complete gonadal dysgenesis, Sertoli dysfunction, and progressive testicular failure. Leydig function is often partially preserved, and infertility is common. 46XX individuals can present with primary ovarian insufficiency/ premature ovarian failure, ovarian dysgenesis, and subfertility. Rarely, testicular or ovotesticular disorder of sex development may occur. Individuals typically have normal adrenal function but in rare cases, adrenal insufficiency may be observed in the context of severe-early onset variants.

definition.val: A syndromic disease caused by a variation in the CRYAB gene, and characterized by a spectrum of phenotypes including cardiomyopathy, cataract, and/or myopathy.

A retinal drusen characterized by subretinal deposits located internal to the retinal pigment epithelium, composed of material aggregations in the subretinal space between photoreceptors and the retinal pigment epithelium. These deposits have a bluish-white appearance by biomicroscopy and appear as hyperreflective lesions above the retinal pigment epithelium on optical coherence tomography.

comments: Reticular pseudodrusen are a strong independent risk factor for late age-related macular degeneration and are particularly associated with geographic atrophy and type 3 neovascularization.

definition.val: An infertility disorder caused by variation in the SYCE1 gene. Affected males may present with non-obstructive azoospermia due to maturation arrest or meiotic failure, while affected females may present with primary ovarian insufficiency.

A precancerous condition characterized by accumulation of some molecular alterations necessary for malignant transformation in a clonal proliferation of cells, representing an intermediate stage in carcinogenesis with increased risk of progression to invasive neoplasia.

nodes.lbl: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy

definition.val: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the TSEN2 gene. This condition is associated with intellectual disability, growth delay, hypotonia, motor delay, ataxia, vision issues, cardiac features (including left ventricular hypertrophy), and pulmonary complications (such as acute respiratory distress and edema). It is also linked to brain structural anomalies such as pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, cortical atrophy, and dilated ventricles. Renal features include proteinuria, thrombotic microangiopathy, end-stage kidney disease, and high-severity hypertension.

synonyms.val: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy

definition.val: A rare hypophysitis characterized histologically by mixed inflammatory cell infiltrates consisting of foamy histiocytes, plasma cells, and small round mature lymphocytes infiltrating the anterior pituitary gland. The tissue often contains cystic-like areas of liquefaction filled with lipid-laden macrophages along with lymphocytes and plasma cells.

A hypophysitis exhibiting histologic features of both xanthomatous and granulomatous hypophysitis, characterized by cholesterol clefts, haemosiderin deposits, multinucleated giant cells, macrophage accumulation and fibrous proliferation.
A rare hypophysitis defined histologically by extensive necrosis of pituitary tissue surrounded by lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils.
A rare subtype of split cord malformation characterized by each hemicord contained in its own dural sac, typically with an intervening bony or cartilaginous septum.
A rare subtype of split cord malformation characterized by both hemicords included in the same single dural sac. An intradural intervening mesenchymal septum may be present.
A rare intermediate form of split cord malformation characterized by both hemichords encapsulated in a single dural sac with presence of an incomplete ventral or dorsal bony spur.

Any hereditary disease caused by a variation in the RNU12 gene, resulting in abnormal splicing of pre-mRNA via the minor spliceosome. The phenotypic spectrum includes craniosynostosis-anal anomalies-porokeratosis (CDAGS) syndrome and autosomal recessive spinocerebellar ataxia 33.

A condition characterized by haploinsufficient levels of STAT5 protein due to reduced copy number or expression of the STAT5A and/or STAT5B genes, with consequent attenuation of STAT5-mediated cytokine signalling (including IL-7 and growth hormone pathways). This condition is also associated with altered lymphocyte homeostasis and modified susceptibility to lymphoma development.

A skeletal muscle disorder caused by heterozygous multi-exon in-frame structural variants of TTN (TTNsv) that escape nonsense-mediated decay and result in expression of an internally deleted titin isoform with dominant-negative effects on sarcomere structure and function. Affected individuals typically present with congenital, childhood-onset, or adult-onset proximal and/or distal muscle weakness, often accompanied by joint contractures, and may develop respiratory involvement or cardiomyopathy.

comments: This condition is genetically and mechanistically distinct from TTN loss‑of‑function recessive titinopathies, hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure, and tibial muscular dystrophy (PMID: 37935568).

definition.val: A disorder of sexual differentiation caused by biallelic variation in the MCM9 gene. Affected females (46,XX) may present with primary ovarian insufficiency or ovarian dysgenesis with short stature; affected males (46,XY) may present with non-obstructive azoospermia due to meiotic failure. Biallelic MCM9 variants have also been associated with predisposition to early-onset colorectal cancer, polyposis, gastric cancer, and germ cell tumors.

nodes.lbl: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QC

definition.val: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QC gene.

synonyms.val: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QC

nodes.lbl: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QB

definition.val: Any systemic lupus erythematosus in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the C1QB gene.

synonyms.val: systemic lupus erythematosus related to C1QB

definition.val: An occupational illness caused by transdermal absorption of nicotine from handling wet, uncured tobacco leaves, presenting with nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, weakness, and other autonomic symptoms. Predominantly affects tobacco farmworkers during harvesting, topping, and curing activities.

comments: Green tobacco sickness is a well-characterized occupational disease affecting an estimated 8 million people worldwide (PMID:30650314), with prevalence ranging from 8.2–47% among tobacco harvesters (PMID:29618907). It has a distinct etiology (transdermal nicotine absorption), risk factor profile, and clinical presentation that distinguishes it from other forms of nicotine poisoning.

nodes.lbl: BLOC1S1-related complex neurodevelopmental disorder with leukodystrophy

definition.val: Any complex neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variationn in the BLOC1S1 gene. The disorder is characterized by intellectual disability, global developmental delay, leukodystrophy, optic atrophy, seizures, abnormal or delayed myelination, and spasticity; some individuals also present with mild features of hypopigmentation and ocular albinism.

synonyms.val: BLOC1S1-related complex neurodevelopmental disorder with leukodystrophy

definition.val: A predisposition to pituitary adenoma due to variation(s) in the AIP gene.

A rare hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy characterized by the inability to perceive physical pain from birth. Affected individuals do not feel pain from injuries, burns, or infections and cannot detect harmful levels of heat, cold, or pressure, which can lead to repeated unrecognized injuries, impaired healing, and serious complications.

A group of neurodevelopmental disorders caused by germline mutations in genes encoding subunits of the Mediator complex, a multi-protein assembly required for RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription. Shared phenotypic features include intellectual disability, speech and language delay, behavioral abnormalities, and variable structural brain anomalies.

A platelet type bleeding disorder of autosomal dominant inheritance caused by a variation in the P2RY12 gene that exerts a dominant negative effect by disrupting receptor homodimerization, leading to markedly impaired adenosine diphosphate induced platelet aggregation despite normal receptor expression. Affected individuals may exhibit severe bleeding symptoms due to defective amplification of platelet activation signals.
A genetic disorder caused by a variation in the GJB2 gene, primarily associated with hearing loss and/or deafness.

Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome caused by the variation in the GP9 gene, marked by absent or markedly reduced GPIb-IX-V complex expression, resulting in impaired platelet adhesion and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Platelets are large and functionally deficient, with severely reduced ristocetin-induced agglutination reflecting loss of functional GPIX within the receptor complex. Variants in GP9 disrupt synthesis or stability of the GPIX subunit, preventing proper assembly of the GPIb-IX-V complex and producing the characteristic bleeding phenotype.

Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GP1BA gene, characterized by macrothrombocytopenia, reduced or absent expression of the GPIb-IX-V complex, and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Affected individuals have large platelets with defective ristocetin-induced agglutination, reflecting the absence or dysfunction of GPIbα on the platelet surface. Variants in GP1BA impair production, trafficking, or incorporation of GPIbα into the receptor complex, preventing normal surface assembly and leading to the classic BSS adhesion defect.

Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome caused by deficiency or dysfunction of GPIbβ, leading to markedly decreased GPIb-IX-V surface expression and impaired platelet adhesion. Platelets are enlarged and poorly responsive to ristocetin, consistent with severe reduction of the assembled receptor complex. Variants in GP1BB affect production or proper folding of the GPIbβ subunit, preventing formation of the full receptor complex and resulting in the characteristic Bernard-Soulier phenotype.
Any disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the AARS2 gene.

Any ectodermal dysplasia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the EDA gene. Key features are hypohidrosis and hypotrichosis; the condition is also characterized by skin anomalies such as soft, thin, and dry skin, eczema, and pigmentation anomalies, as well as fine or brittle hair, dental anomalies such as hypodontia or oligodontia, vocal hoarseness, and hyperthermia susceptibility.

Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, encompassing a phenotypic spectrum that ranges from mild cerebellar ataxia with developmental delay to severe epileptic encephalopathy.

Any genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, characterized by profound developmental delay, microcephaly, intractable epilepsy, and cerebellar hypoplasia.

Any nervous system disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SCN2A gene, which encodes the Nav1.2 sodium channel critical for neuronal function. SCN2A-related disorders span a broad phenotypic spectrum, from self-limited familial neonatal-infantile epilepsy through severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathies to later-onset epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability without seizures, and episodic ataxia. Because Nav1.2 is essential for brain development as well as neuronal excitability, the presentation is predominantly neurodevelopmental where developmental delay, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder are the most consistent features across the spectrum, present even in the absence of seizures. Clinical severity is broadly associated with the functional effect of the variant on the Nav1.2 channel, with gain-of-function changes typically linked to early severe epilepsy and loss-of-function changes more often associated with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability or intellectual disability, although these relationships are complex and not fully understood.

nodes.lbl: EIF2B1-related permanent neonatal diabetes with transient liver dysfunction

definition.val: Any permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the EIF2B1 gene, often accompanied by transient liver dysfunction.

synonyms.val: EIF2B1-related permanent neonatal diabetes with transient liver dysfunction

definition.val: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCAL12 gene.

An ultra-rare hereditary neurological disorder caused by a variation in the IMPDH2 gene, which encodes a key enzyme involved in guanine nucleotide biosynthesis and purine metabolism. The phenotype spans a spectrum from neurodevelopmental delay, intellectual disability, dystonia, tremor, and other movement abnormalities, with variable expressivity and age of onset.

synonyms.val: dominant juvenile-onset dystonia-tremor disorder due to IMPDH2 variants
neurodevelopmental disorder with dystonia due to IMPDH2 deficiency

definition.val: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of genes in the sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway (GLI2, BOC, PTCHD2, and MYCN).
An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of the MYC gene.
An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of melanosomal genes (TYR, TYRP, MITF, and OTX2).

A central nervous system mesenchymal non-meningothelial tumor with a broad morphological spectrum, characterized by fusion of a FET family gene (usually EWSR1 and rarely FUS) with a member of the CREB family of transcription factors (CREB1, ATF1, or CREM). It includes entities previously termed intracranial angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma or intracranial myxoid mesenchymal tumor. It is usually located in the supratentorial brain and mostly affects children and young adults. There is a spectrum of clinical behaviors ranging from slowly growing tumors to rapid recurrences, and rarely metastases.

synonyms.val: intracranial mesenchymal tumor with FET-CREB fusion

nodes.lbl: desmoplastic myxoid tumor of the pineal region, SMARCB1-mutant

definition.val: A pineal body neoplasm that is a SMARCB1-deficient tumor of the brain, characterized by the presence of spindled and epithelioid cells with low-grade morphology that are embedded in a desmoplastic stroma alternating with various extents of loose myxoid matrix.

A very rare, nonrhabdoid, intraventricular tumor with relatively favorable prognosis. It is characterized by the presence of neuroepithelial cells forming cribriform patterns, trabeculae, epithelial membrane antigen immunopositivity on epithelial surfaces, and loss of nuclear INI1 expression.
An adult Refsum disease in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PHYH gene.

synonyms.val: adult Refsum disease due to PHYH
hereditary sensory and motor neuropathy type 4

definition.val: An ovarian serous carcinoma characterized by low-grade cytologic features, infrequent mitotic figures and slow tumor growth, which is thought to develop from a serous borderline ovarian tumor. It shows an activated mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway with KRAS and BRAF mutations and only rarely TP53 mutations, and is a distinct entity from high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma rather than a grade of it. It accounts for 2-5% of ovarian carcinomas and 5-10% of serous ovarian carcinomas.

A phenylketonuria in which blood phenylalanine concentrations do not fall substantially (conventionally defined as a reduction of more than 30%) in response to an oral tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4; sapropterin dihydrochloride) loading test, so that treatment with BH4 is not effective and phenylalanine-restricted dietary management remains necessary.

A disorder of phenylalanine metabolism caused by biallelic variants in the PAH gene, encompassing the full spectrum of phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency from mild hyperphenylalaninemia, which requires no treatment, to phenylketonuria, in which untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations warrant phenylalanine-restricted dietary treatment.
An ossifying fibroma arising predominantly in children and young adults, comprising two histological variants: juvenile trabecular ossifying fibroma and psammomatoid ossifying fibroma.

A juvenile ossifying fibroma predominantly arises in children and adolescents. It is characterized by prominent osteoid formation rimmed by osteoblasts in a fibrotic stroma. Patients usually present with painless jaw expansion that is associated with rapid growth and tooth displacement.

comments: Amplifications of MDM2 and RASAL1 genes have been detected in some cases. Recurrences have been reported in a minority of cases.

definition.val: A juvenile ossifying fibroma arises usually affects individuals in their second to fourth decades with no sex predilection. It is characterized by the presence of multiple ossicles resembling psammoma bodies in a hypercellular stroma.

comments: Recurrences following surgical excision have been reported in a minority of cases.

definition.val: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCB1 gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to schwannomas, meningiomas, rhabdoid tumors and other rare types of tumors. The phenotype correlates with the variant's degree of loss of function: the schwannomatosis phenotype is more commonly observed with partial loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants, while the rhabdoid tumor phenotype is more commonly associated with complete loss-of-function variants.

A neutropenia characterized by persistent absolute neutrophil count below 0.5 x 10^9/L lasting for at least 3 months, not explained by medication use, infection or another underlying condition, and associated with recurrent and potentially life-threatening bacterial infections. The major clinical subtypes include congenital, cyclic, idiopathic, and autoimmune neutropenia, which share common diagnostic evaluation, treatment strategies, and long-term follow-up.

An idiopathic form of severe chronic neutropenia that cannot be classified as congenital, cyclic or autoimmune neutropenia, and is not explained by drug exposure, bone marrow failure, malignancy or systemic autoimmune disease. Symptoms are usually less severe than in congenital neutropenia, but infections can be life-threatening in some patients.

An autoimmune form of severe chronic neutropenia in which neutrophil-specific antibodies increase the destruction of circulating neutrophils, in the absence of systemic autoimmune disease. It is most common in children aged 6 months to 4 years, and it can also occur in adults. Serious bacterial infections are infrequent.

A skeletal system disorder caused by a variation in the GNAS gene, characterized by involvement of the skin, skeleton and certain endocrine organs. Fibrous dysplasia ranges from an isolated monostotic lesion to severe polyostotic disease. McCune-Albright syndrome is diagnosed when fibrous dysplasia occurs with at least one extra-skeletal feature, or when two or more extra-skeletal features occur alone. The condition is not inherited. The signs and symptoms associated with the disorder vary greatly from person to person, depending upon the specific body cells and tissues that are affected by the gene variant.

An optic nerve disorder characterized by ischemic injury to the retrobulbar (posterior) portion of the optic nerve, presenting with sudden visual loss and an initially normal-appearing optic disc, in contrast to anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. It may be arteritic (due to giant cell arteritis), nonarteritic, or surgical (following a surgical procedure).
An optic nerve disorder caused by closed or penetrating trauma to the face or head that injures the optic nerve, resulting in visual loss, often with an afferent pupillary defect.

An optic nerve disorder caused by radiation necrosis of the anterior visual pathway, occurring as a late complication of radiotherapy for head and neck or intracranial tumours and resulting in acute, painless and usually irreversible visual loss. Onset is typically 10 to 20 months after treatment but ranges from 3 months to 9 years.

An optic nerve disorder caused by mechanical compression of the optic nerve or chiasm along its course, for example by orbital or intracranial tumours, sinus mucoceles or thyroid eye disease, resulting in progressive visual loss.

An ocular vascular disorder characterized by acute complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery, a branch of the internal carotid artery, leading to severe ischemia of the globe and associated ocular tissues. It can resemble central retinal artery occlusion with additional choroidal ischemia, and may cause sudden and permanent visual loss.

A vitreous and retinal disorder characterized by incomplete posterior vitreous detachment with persistent focal adhesion to the macula. This exerts anteroposterior traction that distorts foveal anatomy, causing structural changes such as foveal deformation, pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid, with potential progression to a macular hole.

A full-thickness macular hole that results from trauma, such as closed-globe or open-globe ocular injury, laser injury, surgical trauma, lightning strike or electrical shock. It occurs more often in young men, whereas idiopathic macular hole occurs more often in women older than 65 years.

A uveitis occurring in individuals with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and its most frequent extra-articular manifestation. The most common form is chronic anterior uveitis, which is almost always asymptomatic in the initial stages, so screening of at-risk patients is essential.

A glaucoma in which elevation of intraocular pressure results from an identifiable pathophysiological mechanism, such as intraocular inflammation, pigment dispersion, hemorrhage, trauma, corticosteroid use or elevated episcleral venous pressure, in contrast to primary glaucoma. Secondary glaucomas form a heterogeneous group of diseases.

A secondary glaucoma that can develop in pigment dispersion syndrome, in which pigment released from the iris is deposited in the trabecular meshwork, reducing aqueous outflow and raising intraocular pressure, leading to glaucomatous optic neuropathy. It is usually diagnosed between 40 and 50 years of age and occurs more often in men.

A secondary glaucoma in which optic nerve damage results from elevated intraocular pressure secondary to intraocular inflammation via trabecular inflammation/obstruction, steroid response, or synechial angle
closure in the setting of uveitis. Compared with primary open-angle glaucoma, it often has a more aggressive course, with very high intraocular pressure that waxes and wanes.

A secondary glaucoma in which degenerated red blood cells (ghost cells), formed in the vitreous cavity after hemorrhage, pass forward into the anterior chamber and obstruct the aqueous outflow channels.
A secondary glaucoma following intraocular hemorrhage, in which the trabecular meshwork is obstructed by fragments of hemolyzed red blood cells and hemoglobin-laden macrophages.
A secondary glaucoma occurring in individuals with aniridia. Most affected eyes have open anterior chamber angles, and a minority have partial or complete angle closure.

A form of primary angle-closure glaucoma caused by a large or anteriorly positioned ciliary body that leads to mechanical obstruction of the trabecular meshwork. It is most often found in young patients.

A secondary open-angle glaucoma that develops in individuals with exfoliation syndrome. Exfoliation syndrome is associated with raised intraocular pressure in up to 44% of patients, making it the most commonly identifiable cause of secondary open-angle glaucoma.

Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FBN1 gene. This condition is characterized by short stature, delayed bone age, stiff joints, acromegaly, hip dysplasia, respiratory issues (including sleep apnea and asthma), short hands/feet, and facial anomalies (such as a long philtrum, bulbous nose, broad/depressed nasal bridge, thick lips, and elongation of the eyelashes).
Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CAMK2A gene.

Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the NUS1 gene. Biallelic variants cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation. Heterozygous variants, including deletions, cause a complex neurological disorder with developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy including developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and progressive myoclonus epilepsy, and movement disorders including myoclonus, dystonia, ataxia, tremor and parkinsonism. Rare NUS1 variants have also been associated with Parkinson's disease.

A multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome caused by homozygous loss-of-function variants in the ABL1 gene. It is characterized by multiple congenital malformations (wormian skull bones and brachydactyly) and distinctive facial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, prominent eyes, short, broad and flat nose, and macrostomia). It is allelic to, but clinically distinct from, congenital heart defects and skeletal malformations syndrome, which is caused by germline gain-of-function variants in ABL1.

Any tubulinopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TUBB gene. Heterozygous TUBB variants cause two overlapping developmental disorders, complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) and congenital symmetric circumferential skin creases (CSCSC), also known as circumferential skin creases Kunze type. The clinical findings are diverse and include abnormalities of the cortex, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brain stem and cerebellum, microcephaly, intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, excess skin folding and growth retardation.

An acrodermatitis characterized by the acute onset of a self-limited, symmetrical, monomorphic papular or papulovesicular eruption predominantly on the cheeks, buttocks and extensor surfaces of the extremities, with relative sparing of the trunk. It mainly affects children between 1 and 6 years of age and is considered an immunologic reaction triggered by viral infections, most commonly Epstein-Barr virus and hepatitis B virus, or occasionally by vaccination. Lesions typically resolve spontaneously within weeks without scarring.

A salivary gland adenocarcinoma that arises predominantly from the minor salivary glands, most often in the palate, and rarely from the major salivary glands. It is characterized by cytologic uniformity and architectural diversity, with tumor cells showing pale to clear nuclei with inconspicuous nucleoli arranged in a wide variety of growth patterns. It commonly harbors a PRKD1 E710D mutation, typically presents as a painless, slow-growing mass, and generally has an excellent prognosis.

An eating disorder characterized by avoidance or restriction of food intake due to one or more of the following: lack of interest in eating or food, sensitivity to sensory characteristics of food (such as taste, texture, smell, or appearance), or concern about aversive consequences of eating (such as choking or vomiting), resulting in persistent failure to meet appropriate nutritional and/or energy needs as manifested by significant weight loss, nutritional deficiency, dependence on enteral feeding or nutritional supplements, or marked interference with psychosocial functioning, and where the eating disturbance is not better explained by lack of available food, cultural or religious practices, another mental disorder, or a concurrent medical condition.

A form of diabetes mellitus unique to individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF), arising primarily from progressive fibrotic destruction of the pancreas leading to insulin deficiency, with additional contributions from insulin resistance. CFRD affects approximately 20% of adolescents and 40-50% of adults with CF. It shares features with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes but is a distinct clinical entity with its own diagnostic criteria and management guidelines.

A disease associated with CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) dysfunction that does not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis (CF). CFTR-related disorders are characterized by clinical evidence of CFTR dysfunction limited to a single organ system, a sweat chloride concentration below the CF diagnostic threshold (typically less than 60 mmol/L), and CFTR genotypes that often include at least one variant not classified as CF-causing. Recognized CFTR-related disorders include congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD), acute recurrent or chronic pancreatitis, and disseminated bronchiectasis.

comments:
A CFTR-related disorder is defined as a clinical entity with evidence of CFTR dysfunction in at least one organ system that **does not meet** the diagnostic criteria for CF. Typically this means:
- Sweat chloride below the CF diagnostic threshold (<60 mmol/L)
- Clinical involvement limited to a single organ system
- CFTR genotype that includes at least one variant not classified as CF-causing

See 'cystic fibrosis' (MONDO:0009061) for diagnosis criteria for CF.

definition.val: A liver disorder that arises as a consequence of cystic fibrosis. Cystic fibrosis-related liver disease encompasses a spectrum of hepatobiliary abnormalities caused by CFTR dysfunction in cholangiocytes, including focal biliary cirrhosis, multilobular biliary cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, and cholangiopathy. It is a significant cause of non-pulmonary morbidity and mortality in CF, affecting approximately 5-10% of CF patients.

definition.val: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by hypofibrinogenemia and variable liver disease (ranging from asymptomatic transaminase elevation to cirrhosis), caused by variants in FGG that lead to retention of variant fibrinogen as eosinophilic inclusions within the hepatocellular endoplasmic reticulum.

An Ehlers-Danlos syndrome characterized by skin hyperextensibility with velvety skin texture and absence of atrophic scarring, generalized joint hypermobility with or without recurrent dislocations, and easily bruised skin or spontaneous.

A rare systemic disease for which two subtypes exist, either related to the gene PLOD1 or FKBP14, and for which the clinically overlapping characteristics include congenital muscle hypotonia, congenital or early-onset kyphoscoliosis (progressive or non-progressive), and generalized joint hypermobility with dislocations/subluxations (in particular of the shoulders, hips, and knees). Additional features which may occur in both subtypes are skin hyperextensibility, easy bruising of the skin, rupture/aneurysm of a medium-sized artery, osteopenia/osteoporosis, blue sclerae, umbilical or inguinal hernia, chest deformity, marfanoid habitus, talipes equinovarus, and refractive errors. Gene-specific features, with variable presentation, are additionally observed in each subtype.

A HOXA1-related syndrome characterized by horizontal gaze palsy, sensorineural deafness, central hypoventilation, developmental delay, and intellectual disability, described in persons of Athabaskan American Indian heritage. Swallowing dysfunction, vocal cord paralysis, facial paresis, seizures, internal carotid artery, and cardiac outflow tract anomalies may be additionally observed. No dysmorphic facial features are associated.
An infection of the intervertebral disk space.
Discitis caused by infection with Staphylococcus.
Discitis caused by infection with Escherichia coli.
Discitis caused by infection with Streptococcus pneumoniae.
Discitis caused by infection with Salmonella.
Discitis caused by infection with fungi.

A congenital autosomal dominant immune deficiency characterized by abnormal retention of mature neutrophils in the bone marrow (myelokathexis) and occasional hypogammaglobulinemia, associated with an increased risk for bacterial infections and a susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) induced lesions (cutaneous warts, genital dysplasia and invasive mucosal carcinoma).
This syndrome is characterized by the association of intellectual deficit, congenital cataract, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

A disorder caused by the presence of autoantibodies directed against phospholipids, causing a hypercoaguable state, which may result in blood clots, stroke, heart attack, and in women, significant pregnancy-related complications, including miscarriage and still birth. The syndrome is often associated with other autoimmune disorders, most commonly lupus erythematosus, and infections, including syphilis and Lyme disease.
A form of chronic intestinal pseudoobstruction caused by a developmental failure of the enteric neurons to differentiate or migrate properly and manifests as a bowel obstruction.

synonyms.val: pseudoobstruction chronic idiopathic intestinal neuronal type

synonyms.val: neurologic, endocrine, and pancreatic disease, multisystem, infantile-onset
infantile-onset multisystem neurologic, endocrine, and pancreatic disease

definition.val: Autosomal dominant form of antiphospholipid syndrome.
Any 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the DHX37 gene.

Idiopathic recurrent vertigo associated with positional nystagmus. It is associated with a vestibular loss without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in labyrinthitis and vestibular neuronitis inflammation in the ear is not observed.

A rare, primary immunodeficiency. It is caused by a currently undetermined defect in the Fas-induced apoptosis pathway. No mutations in Fas, FASLG or CASP10 are detectable. Disruption of Fas-induced apoptosis impairs lymphocyte homeostasis and immune tolerance. Characteristic laboratory findings include an increase in circulating, double-negative (CD4-/CD8-) T cells in the setting of immune-mediated anemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia. Clinical signs present in childhood include fatigue, pallor, bruising, hepatosplenomegaly and chronic, non-malignant, non-infectious lymphadenopathy. The clinical course is influenced by a strong association with other autoimmune disorders and an increased risk for developing Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
